🌊🇲🇽 <u>The Gulf of Mexico Is Running a Fever</u>

The Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean held 29-31°C through July as a marine heat wave struck Mexico's Pacific coast, Contralínea reports. Mexico's National Meteorological Service and Civil Protection now forecast 18-21 cyclones this Pacific season, threatening operations at the ports of Manzanillo and Lázaro Cárdenas and straining power generation in water-scarce regions, while Quintana Roo's reef-dependent tourism economy faces thermal stress already detected in nearby waters.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Builds Its Own Electric Workhorse</u>

Olinia Carga — Mexico's homegrown electric cargo vehicle developed by the IPN, UNAM and TecNM — reaches the market in late 2027 at around 150,000 pesos, hauling 650 kg over 120 km on a charge from a standard wall outlet. Project director Roberto Capuano Tripp says it runs at "one-third the cost of a motocarro"; first-year output targets 10,000 units, 8,000 already committed, scaling to 50,000 a year, all built with majority Mexican capital.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Won't Be Washington's Voting Bloc</u>

Mexico abstained on the OAS resolution against Nicaragua, and President Sheinbaum grounded the decision in the Constitution, calling it "a matter of self-determination." The measure passed 29-1 — Brazil the lone no — with Mexico abstaining; Sheinbaum stressed the stance follows constitutional principles of non-intervention, not the personal preference of envoy Alejandro Encinas, and ruled out lecturing Managua on democracy: "it is a decision of the Nicaraguans themselves."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PRI Boss Alito Faces the Reckoning</u>

Campeche's anti-corruption prosecutor will bring 32 ex-officials from PRI leader Alito Moreno's governorship before a judge for allegedly siphoning more than 270 million pesos through shell companies across 12 state agencies; 17 collaborators are already under arrest. The alleged peculado ran through the Public Security, Health, Tourism and Education secretariats over five years — while Alito now tours Washington demanding sanctions on his own country.

‍MEXICO NEWS DAILY: A Morelos narco ranch becomes a school and health center August 20, 2026 | 📵 📰 "La Barbie's" seized ranch El Paraíso in Atlacholoaya will house an agricultural high school, a traditional-medicine center, and an office for Indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities. US coverage: zero. 🇲🇽 The gringo press ran the seized cartel ranches wall-to-wall in 2025. A ranch turned into a classroom doesn't fit the frame. • Seized in 2009; won as a lottery prize the winner refused, then sold back to the state. • Three new entities: high school, traditional medicine, Indigenous-affairs office.

text: ‍RIO TIMES: Mexico's Economy Is Tracking 2.7% in a Year, Not 0.1% August 20, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Headlines led with a "0.1%" July figure — the seasonally adjusted month-on-month blip — and read it as stagnation. The annual pace actually accelerated to 2.7% y/y, up from 2.0% in June. 🇲🇽 Same data, two very different stories depending on which number goes in the headline. • "The 0.1% is the seasonally adjusted change from June to July." • Annual growth: 2.7% in July vs 2.0% in June.

‍NEWSNATION: Migrant caravan heads north through Mexico to US southern border August 20, 2026 | 🔴 📰 NewsNation and Hannity ran the old script — a "caravan heading north" toward the border. The ~500–600 people who left Tapachula on Aug 20 said their destination is Mexico City, to regularize status and work in Mexico, not to cross into the US. 🇲🇽 Border crossings are down roughly 80% since 2025; organizers openly say this caravan isn't US-bound. • Headline: "heads north through Mexico to US southern border" • Mexican reporting: "it's not US-bound"

text: WSJ: Mexico's Press Is Still Free Under Sheinbaum August 19, 2026 | 🟢 📰 The WSJ ran Mary O'Grady's "Sheinbaum Moves to Gag Mexico's Media" — then printed the government's reply on the same opinion page. Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco: Mexico's press "is not silenced." 🔍 Worth noting when it happens: the outlet that swung gave the target space to answer with evidence. • "It is not a matter of rhetoric. It is a matter of evidence, and the facts contradict her claim." • Velasco: Mexico is living "the freest and most democratic moment in its history." Source

🇲🇽📈 <u>THE PESO BROKE BELOW 17 TO THE DOLLAR</u>

The peso closed Thursday at 16.9573 per dollar, its strongest level since 2024, and is up 5.8 percent against the dollar so far in 2026, El Financiero reports. Sheinbaum credited a "very solid economy" and international confidence: "If there were no international confidence in the Mexican economy, the peso would not be where it is." The strength cuts both ways, importers and firms carrying dollar debt gain, while remittance recipients, tourism and oil revenue lose ground.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>US COURT THROWS OUT WASHINGTON'S ORDER TO BREAK UP AEROMÉXICO-DELTA</u>

A US appeals court struck down the Department of Transportation's move to dissolve the Aeroméxico-Delta joint venture, calling the demand disproportionate and arbitrary and restoring the antitrust immunity the airlines had been granted. DOT had branded the alliance "legalized collusion" and pointed to the roughly 60 percent of cross-border flights the two carriers control, but the airlines showed Washington applied stricter standards to them than to comparable joint ventures in Asia. Schedules, fares and capacity stay coordinated.
